sections.h2: What will I find at the Holmes County Recorder's office on Clinton Street?
sections.html:
The Recorder keeps Holmes County's land records at 75 E. Clinton Street, Suite 101, Millersburg, OH 44654. Phone (330) 674-5916, fax (330) 674-0782. A card, a check or cash all work at the counter, deeds included, according to the county's overview page.

Holmes County was cut from Coshocton, Tuscarawas and Wayne counties in 1824, and Millersburg became its seat. The overview page lists the records held in Suite 101:

  • deeds, mortgages and leases
  • liens for mechanics, workers' compensation, unemployment and federal taxes
  • partnerships, UCC financing statements and soldier's discharges
  • plats

Most sellers touch only two of these, the deed they sign and any mortgage release the lender files after payoff.

sections.h2: Why does a Holmes County deed visit so many offices first?
sections.html:
Because Holmes County's conveyance standards, effective March 1, 2019, demand a description review before the Auditor or Recorder sees the paper. Tax Map Office approval is mandatory for every legal description, plat, land contract, mineral deed and access easement.

The county is rural to its core: the Census Bureau reported under 0.1% of residents living in urban areas in 2020, and Wikipedia says about 48% of residents were Amish that year, the densest Amish population anywhere. Farm tracts that pass between families often carry old metes and bounds wording, and that is what the Tax Map staff read line by line. In the 2020 to 2024 data the average household here holds 3.26 people, far above the 2.29 to 2.50 range in Huron, Jackson and Jefferson counties.

Budget one workday for each submission. The standards promise 24 hours between drop-off and pick-up, with longer waits for complex files. A draft can be reviewed early, which keeps the signed deed from bouncing.

sections.h2: In what order do the Holmes County offices handle a deed?
sections.html:
The conveyance-by-mail sheet sets out four stops. Each has its own forms and fees, and mailed paper needs a stamped, pre-addressed envelope for every stop.

StepOfficeLocationRole
1Tax Map Office75 E. Clinton St., Suite 102, (330) 674-6631Reviews the description, 24-hour period
2Planning Commission2 Court St., Suite 2, (330) 674-8625Stamps papers that need its approval
3County Auditor75 E. Clinton St., Suite 107Collects conveyance and transfer fees
4County Recorder75 E. Clinton St., Suite 101Records the deed

Source: Holmes County conveyance-by-mail instructions. The Auditor looks for the Tax Map and Planning Commission stamps before touching a file, so a skipped stop freezes everything behind it.

sections.h2: What does the Holmes County Auditor take from a seller?
sections.html:
The fee schedule in the county standards prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of sale price as the conveyance fee and $0.50 for each parcel on the document as the transfer fee. That schedule is dated January 1, 1989, so confirm both numbers with the Auditor before you set a closing date. State law assigns the bill to the grantor, meaning the seller (R.C. 319.202(D)).

  • Write the check to the Holmes County Auditor and send recording fees separately.
  • The office returns no change on an overpaid check and will not accept a signed blank check.
  • A check stopped on a transfer is referred to the county Prosecutor.
  • Attach form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Homestead property adds DTE 101 and current agricultural use land adds DTE 102.

Moving a mobile home title takes one more stamp. The Auditor will not process that transfer until the Treasurer's stamp shows the home's taxes are paid.

sections.h2: What will the Holmes County Recorder bill for a deed?
sections.html:
The latest fee notice on the Recorder's announcements page is dated 2019. It set most documents at $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that, citing R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. Senate Bill 94 later amended the statute, effective October 24, 2024, so a county may now tack on a preservation surcharge of as much as five dollars. Phone the office for the total on your page count.

Formatting can raise the bill. R.C. 317.114 sets the layout, and a nonconforming paper is still recorded for an extra $10.00 service charge plus a $10.00 housing trust fund charge. The layout calls for:

  • 10-point type or larger in black or blue ink, with no highlighting
  • pages between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches
  • one inch of margin at each side and the foot of every page
  • three blank inches at the head of page one, and an inch and a half on later pages

The rule skips court and taxing-authority papers, plats, DD-214s and state or federal documents.

sections.h2: How do I search Holmes County records or e-record a deed?
sections.html:
Two search tools sit on the Recorder's page. AVA needs no login and fits a one-time lookup. Laredo Anywhere is for people who search often, and the county posts a setup guide in its document library. Both show images of deeds, easements, rights-of-way and leases. Other record types can be viewed from 1980 forward, and plats live on the Tax Map Department website.

The office accepts documents electronically, including deeds. It names four vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services and CSC, which serve title companies, law firms and banks that record regularly. State law (R.C. 317.13) gave every recorder until June 30, 2026 to offer electronic filing of conveyance papers, and that deadline is behind us.

sections.h2: Can I get a warning if someone files a paper against my Holmes County property?
sections.html:
The Recorder's overview page invites owners to sign up for Property Fraud Alert and points to a flyer in the Recorder section of the county document library. An alert matters most to an owner who lives away from the house or who has just inherited it, because a forged deed or an unexpected lien only shows up in the public record after it is filed.

Once a sale closes, the same office record becomes the buyer's proof of ownership. Check that the deed shows the correct parcel, the Tax Map Office stamp and the Auditor's endorsement before anything is handed over.

sections.h2: What do Holmes County's housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 44,970 residents for July 2025, which is 1.7% above the April 2020 base. There are 14,592 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 it puts the owner-occupied rate at 79.0%, the middle owner-occupied home at $267,700 and median household income at $76,140.

Two other figures explain why paper filing persists. Just 63.5% of households report a broadband subscription, the thinnest coverage in that four-county table, and 49.0% of people five and older speak something other than English at home. Calling or visiting Suites 101, 102 and 107 often beats an online form.

Visitors help the local economy. Wikipedia says Holmes drew the second most tourists of any Ohio county in 2017, with the Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center in Berlin among the stops.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Holmes County Recorder by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. The overview page states that the office accepts cash, check and credit card, and says the same applies to deeds and other conveyance documents.

faqs.q: Is Tax Map approval needed before a Holmes County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: Yes, whenever the paper carries a legal description. The standards route all descriptions, land contracts, mineral deeds and easements to the Tax Map Office first, with a 24-hour review.

faqs.q: Who owes the conveyance fee on a Holmes County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor, and the Auditor's schedule prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of price plus $0.50 per parcel, dated January 1, 1989. Verify the figures with the Auditor.

faqs.q: Can a Holmes County deed go through the mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Follow the four-stop sheet in order, and enclose forms, fees and a pre-addressed, correctly stamped envelope for each office.

faqs.q: Who can obtain a recorded military discharge in Holmes County?
faqs.a: Only authorized parties, such as the veteran, a county veterans service officer or the heir of a deceased veteran. A discharge stays out of the public record for 75 years, and anyone else sees just name, rank, birth date, discharge date and type.
